title: Notable recent biology and biomedical papers on arXiv — 2026-10-22
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is a relevance-ranked selection, not a popularity ranking; citation or download/view popularity is not established. arXiv's biomedical coverage is incomplete relative to bioRxiv, medRxiv, and the wider literature.

sections.title: RiboBridge: protein-conditioned de novo RNA binder structure design
sections.abstract: RiboBridge separates RNA conformation generation from protein–RNA assembly and evaluates predicted complex structures on a temporally split, filtered benchmark of 124 protein–RNA complexes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved structural recovery versus compared methods, including best fNAT and DockQ and lowest interface/ligand RMSDs on their benchmark; native information is used only after generation to select among predicted-pocket candidates.
sections.unique_caveat: Computational structural prediction does not establish experimental binding or function. The authors identify interface-hypothesis prioritization and sequence realization as unresolved and call for functional validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Strong molecular/RNA relevance, q-bio.BM cross-list, and a reported 124-complex benchmark with component ablations; relevance evidence, not an attention or citation signal.

sections.title: Benchmarking Recent Single-Cell Synthetic Data Generation Methods on the OneK1K Dataset
sections.abstract: The paper compares scGFT, scLDM, and Cell2Sentence on donor-split OneK1K single-cell RNA-seq data (633,711 training cells from 490 donors; 634,022 test cells from 491 donors) across fidelity, biological preservation, and membership-inference risk.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that copying non-highly-variable-gene expression can expose donor membership, while Poisson-based reconstruction reduces that risk; scGFT and scLDM preserve more biological structure than an independent Poisson baseline in their tests.
sections.unique_caveat: Modeling is restricted to highly variable genes with reconstructed background expression; authors note dataset sparsity, metric sensitivity, and need to assess full-gene behavior. One dataset does not establish privacy in other cohorts.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct genomics and single-cell relevance; three generators assessed on donor-split OneK1K for both biological utility and membership-inference risk; arXiv comment says presented at CAMDA 2026 ELSA Health Privacy Challenge.

sections.title: Supercoiling Drives DNA-Protein Co-Condensation
sections.abstract: Coupled DNA-elasticity and protein-concentration modeling suggests that supercoiling can promote DNA–protein co-condensation by coupling protein wetting to DNA twist-to-writhe conversion.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' model predicts that supercoiling can lower a nucleation barrier and enable co-condensation that otherwise remains kinetically trapped, proposing DNA topology as a control parameter.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is theoretical/computational, not a new cellular or biochemical demonstration; the proposed causal pathway needs targeted experimental testing.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in biomolecular research and directly addresses genome organization; combines theoretical analysis and simulations and relates model energy scales to prior single-molecule measurements.

sections.title: AI Enhanced Cerenkov Luminescence Microscopy
sections.abstract: A Monte Carlo-guided image-restoration model trained on simulated tumor-spheroid images is evaluated on experimental Cerenkov luminescence microscopy images from 27 U87 spheroids.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report lower reconstruction error for CARE than Noise2Void on synthetic validation data and improved localization, contrast, and signal-to-noise measures when applying CARE to experimental images.
sections.unique_caveat: Paired ground truth is simulated; results on 27 spheroids do not establish diagnostic accuracy, clinical utility, or performance across scanners, tracers, and tumor models.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct biomedical imaging application with a reported 15,360 paired synthetic images from 80 simulated geometries and an experimental-image application set of 27 spheroids.

sections.title: Direct Production of Ultra-High Radioisotopic Pure $^{64}$Cu from Natural Zinc Metal via D-D Fusion Narrowband Fast Neutron Source Irradiation
sections.abstract: The authors irradiate natural zinc with a deuterium–deuterium fusion neutron source and use time-resolved gamma spectroscopy to assess the resulting copper radioisotopes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report no-carrier-added $^{64}$Cu from natural zinc, with $^{64}$Cu the only copper radioisotope detected in the sample and a threshold-corrected radioisotopic-purity estimate of 99.97%.
sections.unique_caveat: A production-method demonstration, not an efficacy or patient study; reproducibility, radiochemical labeling, batch yield, and downstream biological performance are not established by the reported experiment.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Biomedical radiopharmaceutical-production relevance and direct irradiation/spectroscopy experiment; abstract specifies one-hour irradiation and 72-hour measurement.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: Structure-first RNA binder design remains bounded by experimental function (RiboBridge); synthetic single-cell data exposes a privacy-utility trade-off shaped by non-HVG handling and metric choice (OneK1K); DNA topology is modeled as a mechanism for genome organization but remains theoretical (Supercoiling); translational imaging and isotope-production studies combine simulation with limited experimental evidence and do not establish clinical benefit (Cerenkov microscopy; 64Cu production).

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: Follow RiboBridge structure prediction with blinded biochemical binding assays and sequence-realizability tests; test single-cell synthetic-data privacy across independent donor-held-out cohorts and full-gene settings; experimentally vary DNA supercoiling while measuring condensation thresholds and reversibility; validate Cerenkov restoration on independent image sets; and repeat 64Cu production while measuring yield and radiochemical as well as radionuclidic quality. These are proposed follow-ups, not demonstrated outcomes.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The most directly biology-focused work is computational RNA design, synthetic single-cell data, and a physical model of DNA condensation. Imaging and radiochemistry show early-stage technical results but no clinical validation. With no defensible attention signal for this fresh batch, these are notable recent papers rather than measured arXiv trends.
